title: CHIMERUNE — a browser creature battler built with AI tools. Looking for feedback on the first few fights.
author: Due_Entertainer7020
selftext:
Hey everyone, I’m working on CHIMERUNE, a browser game where you collect creatures, reforge them into stronger forms, and fight through Story encounters and bosses. This is for a game jam I participated in and i want to make sure i have it as polished as possible before the close of editing which is in 2 days

AI tools have helped with code, and artwork. Playtesting has exposed things a good-looking screenshot misses, like UI that became too small when players maximized the game. That’s the kind of issue I’ve been correcting in the current polish pass.

If you try the first few fights, I’d love to know where the momentum drops or anything feels unclear. What would make you want another session?

For other devs using AI: what has helped you keep the whole game feeling consistent as you add more content?

Play: [https://run.world/coshus/chimerune](https://run.world/coshus/chimerune)

comments.author: office-canard
comments.body: For me it's deciding the core first and never letting anything else lead. I settle the rules and the feel before anything else, and every piece of content I add after that has to serve them. Story, setting and art are there to make the rules shine, not the other way around. When I ask AI for new content, I describe what the core needs, not just what the new thing should look like. Content that doesn't serve the core gets cut, even if it looks good. Good luck with the jam!

replies.author: Due_Entertainer7020
replies.body:
I appreciate the feedback. I wish I had more time to make the proper adjustments. A friend of mine just suggested today to see if I could get feedback on Reddit so I appreciate it.

If you played it what would you change about the start? I tried to go with the story and then lead to a tutorial for the basic controls and then afterward the main core which is the reforging.

replies.author: office-canard
replies.body: To be honest I haven't played it yet, so this is just how I'd approach it. I'd put the core first. Let the player do one reforge in the first minute, before most of the story, and teach the rest one step at a time as it's needed. The story hits harder once people already care about their creatures. That might also help with the "too much at once" feeling Guildbound mentioned.

replies.author: Due_Entertainer7020
replies.body: Again thank you for the advice! It is much appreciated.

comments.author: Guildbound
comments.body: Concept and core might be good just feel so much thrown at me at once.

replies.author: Due_Entertainer7020
replies.body: Was the story intro to lengthy? Or was it like the tutorial fight?

replies.author: Guildbound
replies.body: Story, intro fight is medium length you could lower it but what I also felt is the attack animation is to short and to fast maybe lower the fps to 10-12

replies.author: Due_Entertainer7020
replies.body: Ok, I appreciate it. Thanks for taking the time to play and give me some feedback. I’ll definitely take it into consideration for my last update before the entry closes.

replies.author: Guildbound
replies.body: I like the art work, message me again!! When you’ve done changes I’ll play it again.

replies.author: Due_Entertainer7020
replies.body: Hey I was able to implement the majority of the changes that you highlighted and recommended, as far as the feedback of the enemies being hit, better visibility for the attacks, and the animations. When you get a chance, check it out and let me know if you notice the difference and if there's anything else that stands out to you. Again, thanks for the feedback.

comments.author: Guildbound
comments.body: Also I would highly recommend moving away from run.world and practice with real tools so you can see the difference. That way your able to port your game to Steam/app stores etc
